# Assets

An asset is game content several nodes share, or that is too big to
inline in a scene node. This is what Godot calls a Resource.

Content lives in files (or inline in a scene) rather than on a node,
and plugins register asset types the same way they register
components. An `asset`-typed component property names which type it
takes, which is also what gives it an inspector row.

## One rule

**A string is a reference, a table is a definition.** Every
asset-typed property accepts either:

```toml
[nodes.animation]
library = "animations/platform.toml"   # a reference: every node naming it shares one parsed asset

# or, inline:
[nodes.animation.library]
type = "animation_clip"
# ... the definition, written in place
```

An author writes three reference forms and no more:

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"animations/hero.toml"` | The whole file |
| `"animations/hero.toml#run"` | The entry named `run` inside it |
| `"#hero_idle"` | An `[[assets]]` block in the same scene document |

Sharing is the default; `assets.duplicate` opts out with a private
copy. A reference that does not resolve warns and the rest of the
scene loads, so one bad path does not take a whole scene down. A
definition table that does not parse is an error, reported where it
was written.

## Types

Registered by plugins, so this list is whatever the build contains.

| type | project directory |
| --- | --- |
| `animation_clip` | `animations/` |
| `heightfield` | `terrain/` |
| `mesh` | `models/` |
| `tileset` | `tilesets/` |

## The `assets` script module

`directory`, `duplicate`, `exists`, `load`, `reload`, `save`.

## Plugins define asset types

Core never learns what an asset *is*. A plugin registers a parser
with `App::register_asset_type(name, parse)` and downcasts the parsed
object itself.

## Assets ship in packs

`balaur export` bundles them, so a shipped game resolves an asset
exactly as a dev run does. Binary assets (textures, audio, fonts)
travel in the pack too, each carrying a content hash so a truncated
entry is caught rather than handed on.
